The manipulation of time in the story is well-balanced and enhances its emotional depth. In the present timeline, only a couple of hours pass—from "midafternoon" until "evening gathered around them"—as Martin sits beside the crash site. The author stretches this quiet, static waiting period by interweaving it with significant time compression via Martin's memories. Within just a few paragraphs, seven years with his dog, two failed marriages, and a thirty-six-year career as a city planner are concisely summarized through poignant, specific details (like a burned tablecloth or a yellow rectangle of light). This contrast between the stillness of the present moment on the indifferent mountain and the compressed weight of an entire lifetime creates a contemplative, melancholic pacing that fits the narrative's themes of mortality, memory, and loneliness.
